articles.title: Sør-Korea svarer på Trumps utspill
articles.content:
Sør-Korea sier de håper på en meningsfull dialog mellom USA og Nord-Korea.

Tidligere mandag varslet Donald Trump at han har beordret det amerikanske forsvaret til å øve mindre med Sør-Korea.

– Sør-Korea og USA har hatt et tett samarbeid om å bevare en sterk felles forsvarsstilling og felles øvelser og trening. Vi vil fortsette å koordinere tett, heter det i uttalelsen fra presidentkontoret.

Det heter videre at landet nå også vil bidra til arbeidet med å gjenopprette sikkerheten i Hormuz-stredet.

Forholdet mellom Sør- og Nord-Korea

Forholdet mellom Nord-Korea og Sør-Korea er spent. Landene inngikk aldri noen fredsavtale etter Koreakrigen på 1950-tallet.

articles.title: Minst ti personer mistet livet i bussulykke i Brasil
articles.content:
Minst ti personer har mistet livet etter at en buss veltet i et bratt fjellområde nord for Rio de Janeiro søndag. Det opplyser det lokale brannvesenet og brasilianske medier.

Åtte personer døde på ulykkesstedet nær fjellbyen Petrópolis, mens ytterligere to personer døde på sykehus. De omkomne skal være ni kvinner og en ung jente, melder NTB.

Alvorlige bussulykker skjer ofte i Brasil på grunn av krevende veiforhold.

Brasil

President Lula da Silva vant presidentvalget i Brasil i oktober og ble innsatt 1. januar 2023. 8. januar gikk støttespillere av tidligere president Jair Bolsonaro til angrep på Kongressen, presidentpalasset og høyesterett i hoevdstaden Brasília.

articles.title: 2325 mennesker er døde etter å ha blitt smittet med ebola i Kongo
articles.content:
Ebolautbruddet i Kongo har kostet 2325 mennesker livet og er dermed det dødeligste i landets historie, skriver NTB.

Det viser tall fra kongolesiske myndigheter søndag. Dødstallet har passert de 2280 dødsfallene under utbruddet i 2018–2020.

Landets folkehelseinstitutt opplyser at det nå er registrert 4945 bekreftede smittetilfeller. 101 av dem er påvist i løpet av det siste døgnet.

DR Kongo

Den demokratiske republikken Kongo (også kalt Kongo-Kinshasa) ligger i Sentral-Afrika og grenser til SAR og Sør-Sudan i nord, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi og Tanzania i øst, Zambia og Angola i sør og Kongo-Brazzaville i vest.

Ebola

Ebolaepidemien i årene 2013-2015 livet av 11.300 mennesker i de tre vestafrikanske landene Guinea, Sierra Leone og Liberia. Etter at det store utbruddet var over, er det registrert flere sporadiske tilfeller av smitte.

articles.content:

Hele 53 prosent svarer at de har fått trangere økonomi. Samtidig svarer over seks av ti at de er misfornøyde med hvordan Trump håndterer levekostnadene i landet.

Det hvite hus avviser kritikken. En talsperson uttaler til Financial Times at regjeringen jobber for bedre råd ved å kutte skatter og senke prisene på medisin, ifølge NTB.

articles.title: EU planlegger omfattende nye sanksjoner mot Russland
articles.content:
EU vil skjerpe sanksjonene mot Russland betydelig i høst, sier EUs utenrikssjef Kaja Kallas.

– EUs sanksjoner har allerede kostet Russland dyrt og fratatt Russlands krigsmaskin over 1000 milliarder euro. Til høsten legger jeg fram de mest omfattende sanksjonsoppføringene siden krigen startet, sier Kallas til den tyske avisen Die Welt.

Hun sier at dersom tiltakene blir vedtatt, vil antallet russiske enheter som er omfattet av EUs sanksjoner, øke med en tredel.

– Presset må fortsette å øke fram til Moskva avslutter krigen, sier Kallas.

Krigen i Ukraina

articles.content:
Alle nødetater rykker ut etter melding om trafikkulykke i Indre Østfold.

– To biler er involvert, front mot front, skriver operasjonsleder Atle Vesttorp i presseklienten.

– En person erkjenner å ha sovnet bak rattet og dermed kommet over i motgående kjøreretning.

Det skal ha vært en person i hver bil, og klokken 17.45 kan Vesttorp fortelle at begge skal være ute av bilene. Begge skal også være våkne.

– De involverte får hjelp av helsepersonell på stedet, forteller Vesttorp til NRK.

På grunn av hastighen blir begge førerne kjørt til traumemottaket for videre undersøkelser med tanke på høyenergiskader.

Begge bilene har behov for berging, og veien sperres.

articles.title: Jernfjelltunnelen stengt: Bil truffet av stein på størrelse med vaskemaskin
articles.content:
Jernfjelltunnelen på E39 ved Gulen er stengt, etter melding om at en bil er truffet av en stein som falt fra taket.

Steinen beskrives å være på størrelse med en vaskemaskin, og bilen har fått store materielle skader.

– Det skal ha vært to personer og en hund i bilen som ble truffet, de fremstår uskadd. Hendelsen skjedde rundt 500 meter inn i tunnelen fra Knarvik-siden, melder operasjonsleder Knut Dahl-Michelsen.

Jostein Steinsland-Hauge ved 110-sentralen bekrefter.

– Det fremstår som at det har gått bra med de involverte. Bilen er ikke kjørbar.

Tunnelen er tømt for biler og det er uvisst hvor lenge den vil være stengt.

Lise Kristoffersen ved veitrafikksentralen sier det vil bli omkjøringsmulighet via Solheimslia og fylkesvei 571, via ledebil.

Klokken 15.50 skal det ikke være særlig mye kø i området, ifølge Kristoffersen.

articles.title: Tregere salg av sjøhytter: To av tre solgt under prisantydning
articles.content:
Salget av sjøhytter falt i sommer, og to av tre hytter ble solgt under prisantydning, skriver E24.

Mellom juni og august ble det solgt 595 sjøhytter på Finn.no. Det er en nedgang fra i fjor, og nær en halvering sammenlignet med toppåret 2020. Salgene tar også merkbart lengre tid enn før.

Leder for strategi i Finn Eiendom, Eirik Dysthe, påpeker overfor nettavisen at de reelle priskuttene ofte er større enn statistikken viser, fordi manges selgere setter ned prisen i flere omganger før hytta blir solgt.

– Median-kjøperen forhandler seg nå til 4,6 prosent under prisantydning, mens salgssummen lå omtrent på prisantydning under pandemien, sier Dysthe.

Ute i felten merker meglere at kjøperne har god tid.

– Omsetningshastigheten er tregere. Kanskje kan det ta opp til et år å selge, og kanskje skjer salget først neste sommer, sier eiendomsmegler Henning Hesselberg til E24.

Selv om selve salget går tregere, er drømmen om sjøhytte fortsatt sterk.

Sjøhytteannonsene på Finn.no hadde mer enn 10 millioner sidevisninger i sommer, noe som er ny rekord.

articles.title: Sit utsatt for dataangrep
articles.content:
Studentsamskipnaden i Gjøvik, Ålesund og Trondheim (Sit) har vært utsatt for et dataangrep mot kundedatabasen. Det er en risiko for at personopplysninger er på avveier, skriver de i en pressemelding.

De ble informert om angrepet fredag fra systemleverandøren som fortalte at uvedkommende kan ha fått tilgang til personopplysninger.

Opptil 780 studenter med et kundeforhold til Sit kan være berørt. De skal ha blitt varslet.

– Det ble gjennomført tiltak for å stanse aktiviteten og sikre kundedatabasen. Problemet knyttet til dataangrepet er identifisert og rettet, sier administrerende direktør Morten Wolden.

– Angrepet framstår som et forsøk på å tjene penger på SMS-verifisering, og ikke primært for å hente ut persondata, men vi kan ikke stadfeste dette med 100 prosent sikkerhet, sier han.

Søndag 16. august delte Studentsamskipnaden i Gjøvik, Ålesund og Trondheim (Sit) at de har blitt utsatt for et dataangrep.

articles.title: Dødstallene stiger etter jordskjelvet i Indonesia
articles.content:
Antall døde er steget til 51 etter jordskjelvet på øya Flores i Indonesia natt til lørdag. Skjelvet ble målt til 7,7 og hadde episenter i havet utenfor øya Flores.

Rundt 5000 personer er evakuert på grunn av jordras og stengte veier, og mange er send til sykehus med alvorlige skader.

articles.title: 50,000 kroner fine for waking polar bear in Norwegian Arctic
articles.content:
A person in Norway's Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic has been fined 50,000 kroner ($5,255) for using a foghorn to wake a sleeping polar bear, local officials said Thursday.

The incident took place earlier this month when a vessel was sailing in a fjord in northeastern Svalbard, around 1,000 kilometres (620 miles) from the North Pole.

"Its occupants are said to have spotted a polar bear sleeping on land," the governor of the territory said in a statement.

"A person on board then used the ship's foghorn, waking the animal, which moved to another location," he added.

Neither the identity nor nationality of the person has been disclosed.

The governor's office ordered the individual to pay the hefty fine, which the person agreed to do.

Under local regulations "it is forbidden to needlessly disturb, attract or pursue a polar bear", which was declared a protected species in Svalbard in 1972.

Some 260 polar bears were counted in the archipelago during the last scientific estimate, carried out in 2015.

articles.title: 'We truly understand that anxiety': The human side of Norway’s immigration system upgrade
articles.content:
Norway is rebuilding its immigration system through a six-year project. But will it be different this time, and are applicants truly being put first? The Local spoke to Henrik Hansen, Product Lead for the ModUlf project, to learn more.

For years, international residents in Norway have described dealing with immigration authorities as a cold, rigid, and deeply anxious experience.

Authorities are now developing ModUlf, a massive six-year overhaul across the Directorate of Immigration (UDI), the Immigration Appeals Board (UNE), the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (UD), and the police.

It is the Norwegian state’s multi-year initiative to modernise its entire immigration infrastructure and transform the application process for the international community in Norway.

In our previous article, we covered the project's overall goals and what is currently live.

READ ALSO: Inside ModUlf: What's changing in Norway's immigration process?

But as Norway undertakes the major ModUlf project, a key question remains: Does this tech upgrade care about the human side of immigration?

The Local spoke with Henrik Hansen, Product Lead (Produktleder) for the ModUlf project, about user anxiety, potential transition delays, and why officials need input from foreign residents.

When asked whether the technical teams and engineers building these new systems truly care about the stress and anxiety that immigration delays cause applicants, Hansen gave a reassuring-sounding answer.

"I do understand why people worry. It is incredibly difficult to overcome the immigration process as an applicant, so we truly understand that anxiety. But we try to place a major focus on this," Hansen said. "In many of the meetings I am in now, when we're planning, we're always asking: 'How does this feel for the applicant? How does this affect the applicant?' We're always trying to push and think about that, because if you don't actively force yourself to think about it, it's very easy to just design systems that simply improve your own workday."

Hansen explained that in the past, the focus was mostly internal. Now, the development strategy makes teams put the applicant's experience first.

"Improving my day, or the day of a caseworker in UDI, might help a little bit, but in general, we are an organisation which is heavily applicant-focused," he said. "I think, or I hope, we are moving there, focusing more on the human side. We have a good amount of people now who are constantly pushing and making sure that we remember this.”

"It is also a fundamental part of our official mandate,” Hansen further explained. “One of the most important goals of this programme is that we are supposed to make the applicant feel secure. We're supposed to make them self-sufficient, able to do things by themselves where they can clearly understand the process, see what they need to do, and complete it without having to call us or waste hours of time. We want them to understand implicitly what the system is doing, so that's definitely the ultimate goal we are working towards," he said.

READ MORE: Inside ModUlf: How Norway is rebuilding its immigration system

Will these tech upgrades delay current applications?

Many people in the international community worry that UDI processes will take even longer with this six-year upgrade. When asked if this could cause more delays, Hansen responded with transparency.

"I can't say explicitly that delays won't happen, because it's difficult to know everything. So far it has been okay, and we try to implement things without stopping as everything needs to run at the same time in a way. Our methodology is, of course, to avoid affecting applicants as much as we possibly can,” Hansen said.

He explained that even if some applications are still handled by the old system while others use the new one, they cross-reference everything to prevent problems. “But of course it is difficult to make systems, and it might happen in the future," Hansen noted.

Managing a big digital change across the government is also a tough administrative task. Hansen pointed out that running a project with many agencies means balancing very different institutional cultures and ways of working.

“One of our main goals is that it's supposed to feel like one system, even if technically it's a lot of different systems working together," said Hansen.

One of ModUlf's biggest current hurdles is getting foreign residents to share their feedback.

People working on the programme try to conduct interviews and deploy feedback pop-ups, but many applicants are deeply hesitant to participate, Hansen explained.

This is often because people worry that complaining or pointing out problems could hurt their visa status, even though Hansen repeatedly said during the interview that they really need this feedback to better understand users' needs.

“It is difficult to get in touch with applicants. Specifically, for example, applicants who are in the process of appealing a case normally do not want to talk about their case with us. We haven't been able to get them to officially respond because not everyone wants to come to an interview," Hansen said. “For example, when we first made the new digital solution available for the police, we had researchers standing right there in the waiting rooms talking to applicants very informally, asking: 'How did you feel? What did you see? How did it go?' And a lot of people didn't really want to talk to us.”

“We do really want to talk to people, so we try quite hard to be able to do that," Hansen continued. "I don't think we have ever been quite so focused as we are now in talking with our applicants, because in general, our applicants and their experience with our system, is perhaps one of the biggest parts we focus now, because we see that there are quite a lot of complaints or that information is not available. How can we make this easier for our applicants?” wondered Hansen.

He stressed that these user researchers operate completely independently from case-processing personnel, meaning your feedback can never influence the outcome of a residency application.

"My main message is that they should not be scared. We're not going to use your feedback against anyone. The entire point is that we need your help to make good systems that affect applicants positively. So, if you get the opportunity or you receive an email asking for your opinion, please do help us. We really, really want those opinions, because it helps us immensely to adjust. If we don't get that insight, it's very difficult to build good systems for applicants,” said Hansen.

Currently, ModUlf does not have its own feedback portal. You can use the general "Feedback on service" form on UDI.no, which the digital teams check regularly. And, if you are ever approached in person by a researcher at a police station, giving them just five minutes of your time can make a massive difference.

The development teams also closely monitor trends within the UDI telephone support service to pinpoint exactly where applicants are getting confused by the language or user interfaces.

“We also pay close attention to how many people are calling into our telephone service to ask questions. We look closely at the data. Have we got more people calling in now because they don't understand something? Are we getting fewer calls? What is the general content of those calls? Why are they calling us?" Hansen explained.

READ ALSO: 'I am powerless': How waiting for answers from Norway's UDI impacts lives

What does ModUlf mean for applicants in the long run?

The ModUlf project should mark a definitive "before and after" for an immigration system that has felt outdated, rigid, and unfair for far too long.

As many readers have shared with The Local in previous surveys, it often feels unbelievable that such bureaucratic hurdles still persist in 2026; so it is reassuring to see the government actively working to change this situation.

ModUlf should fundamentally redefine how foreign residents interact with the state and, above all, transform their relocation process into a much smoother experience.

By replacing Norway’s crumbling digital foundation, the state hopes to build an immigration infrastructure that can offer predictable timelines, greater transparency, and real-time application tracking.

This change will also mean less need to contact staff, fewer back-and-forth conversations, and fewer frustrating moments where it feels like your outcome depends on which official you get.

Ultimately, international residents hope for much shorter waiting times.

From a human perspective, many applicants simply want to feel that they are not just another anonymous number in a machine, but that they are seen, valued, and that their cases are genuinely being considered.

While technology alone cannot resolve broader geopolitical migration pressures or changing laws, this six-year overhaul is a critical step toward a system that treats applicants openly and fairly, offering reliable and accessible service even during busy times.

Do you think ModUlf will actually make a difference for applicants?

articles.title: Flyplass gjenåpnet på Sicilia
articles.content:
Catania flyplass på den italienske øya Sicilia er gjenåpnet etter å ha vært askestengt. Et vulkanutbrudd på Etna sendte aske opp i lufta og flyplassen har vært stengt siden 8. august. Vulkanen har hyppige utbrudd.

Vulkanen «Etna»

Det er utbot frå den sicilianske vulkanen Etna igjen. Det er Europas mest aktive vulkan, og i desember i fjor blei det registrert 130 jordskjelv etter uvanleg høg aktivitet i vulkanen.

articles.title: Mann død etter sykkelulykke i Oslo
articles.content:
Nødetatene er i Zinoberveien i Sørkedalen i Oslo, etter melding om en alvorlig sykkelulykke.

En mann i 40-årene er bekreftet omkommet etter en alvorlig ulykke i Sørkedalen i Oslo. Kriseteam er påkoblet.

articles.title: Belgia: Skogbrann sprer seg raskt
articles.content:
En skogbrann sprer seg raskt øst i Belgia, nær grensa til Tyskland. Minst 16 kvadratkilometer er ramma, ifølge AFP. Brannmannskap fra både Tyskland og Belgia bidrar. Brannen starta fredag, og har økt kraftig i omfang i løpet av natta. Også brannfly og helikoptre fra EUs sivile beredskap er mobilisert.

Skogbrann og skogbrannfare

Tørt terreng og lite nedbør har ført til stor skogbrannfare

articles.title: What it means to be a 'samboer' and how it can be your ticket to Norway
articles.content:
Being a samboer (cohabitant) in Norway can feel like marriage, but the law often sees it differently. Here is what you need to know before you move in together.

In Norway, saying "I do" in a fancy wedding is becoming less popular and more of an optional extra.

For many, the ultimate relationship goal isn’t a marriage certificate, but the status of samboer (cohabitant).

This is especially true for the international community. Many foreigners either move to Norway to join a Norwegian partner or relocate to the country as a couple and choose to live as de facto partners, proving their status through a shared address.

However, even though samboers are seen almost the same as married couples in society, the legal situation is very different, especially when it comes to taxes and residency rights.

Unlike in countries where such unions feel secondary, in Norway, referring to your partner as your samboer is very common.

It is a perfectly respected, lifelong choice where you can raise a family and share a mortgage without ever stepping into a city hall. In everyday conversation, the word samboer is just as meaningful as "husband" or "wife".

The Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten) defines cohabitation as two people living together in a "marriage-like relationship" without being married.

There is no official registration for cohabitation in Norway. Instead, your status is shown by your address in the National Population Register.

If you need proof that you live together, both of you can order a residence certificate (bostedsattest).

However, cohabitation is not covered by the same laws as marriage. Samboers do not automatically share ownership of their assets.

Because there is no standard legal framework for cohabitation, it is important to enter into a private cohabitation agreement (samboeravtale).

This contract explains who owns what, who is responsible for debts, and how things will be divided if you break up.

While unromantic, it can be necessary to protect your future and many legal services in Norway can help you create the contract.

Registering as a samboer is a valid and accepted way for foreigners to move to Norway.

For people from the EU or EEA, this option is popular because the registration process is simpler within the Schengen area and often has lower or no fees.

READ MORE: How hard is it to pass Norway’s citizenship and social studies tests?

While Norwegians can simply move in together, foreigners must meet strict UDI (the Norwegian Directorate of Immigration) requirements to obtain residency.

Unlike other European countries, Norway requires proof that you have lived together for at least two years.  However, your "ticket" depends on your couple's history.

The first option is the standard Family Immigration permit. This is the most common way for people outside the EU to apply, but it can also be expensive.

In 2026, the application fee for samboers is about 11,900 kroner, and the sponsor (the person who lives in Norway) must show a pre-tax income of at least 416,512 kroner.

This permit gives you rights under the Norwegian Integration Act, like language training, and can lead to permanent residency after three or five years.

The second option is the EU/EEA Residence Card. You can apply for this if you and your Norwegian partner lived together in another EU country while your partner worked or studied there. This is often a "loophole" that many applicants are unaware of.

This application is free, has more flexible rules, and does not require the sponsor to meet a specific income level. However, you must wait 5 years for permanent residency, and you do not have the right to language training.

This option also applies if your partner in Norway is an EU or EEA citizen (but not Norwegian). All the requirements are listed on the UDI website.

Many foreigners think that living together gives them "common law" rights, but this is not the case in Norway.

The law sometimes treats cohabitants like married couples, but in other ways, it treats them as singles.

Each party is considered a single individual with no legal duty to provide financial maintenance for the other. Anything you owned before or bought yourself stays yours.

The financial differences are also clear in the Norwegian tax system. Most of the time, cohabitants are taxed separately and cannot combine deductions as married couples can.

If one partner owns the home, that person pays wealth tax on the full value, even if the other partner has no assets. Married couples are taxed together and get a higher wealth tax threshold.

If you’re cohabitants and have a shared loan, you and your partner have to split the interest based on how much of the debt each of you is responsible for. Usually, unless you have a written agreement, this means each of you claims half of the interest by default. Unlike married couples, you can’t shift these deductions to the person with the higher income to save on taxes.

There is a special category called "spouse-equivalent cohabiting partners" for those with joint children or former spouses with a pension. They can split capital income and expenses, like interest on debt, however they want.

If you and your partner are an international couple running a business together, your tax situation comes down to whether you count as "spouse-equivalent." If you do, you’re allowed to share the income from a joint business, but only in proportion to how much work each of you actually does.

For most other cohabiting couples, you cannot transfer business income to your partner to lower your total tax bill. If only one of you officially owns the business, that person has to report all the profit or loss on their own tax return.

One of the biggest risks for cohabitants is that there is no automatic protection if you break up or if one partner dies.

If you have children under 16 and are separated, you must go to mediation.

If one partner dies, the law only protects cohabitants who have children. They are entitled to a statutory inheritance of 4G (the National Insurance basic amount, or approximately 500,000 kroner) and the legal right to remain in the shared home.

Cohabitants without children do not have any legal right to inherit. If there is no will, your home could go to your partner’s parents or siblings.

Ultimately, a written agreement is the only way to protect yourself from losing everything.

articles.title: Zelenskyj: Ukrainske droner har truffet russisk flybase
articles.content:
Ukrainske droner har angrepet en russisk rakettfabrikk i Samara samt militærflybasen Savasleyka, opplyser president Volodymyr Zelenskyj på Telegram. Ifølge Samaras guvernør Ivan Noskov opplevde luftforsvaret «massive angrep».

Angrepene er ledd i Ukrainas angrep mot russisk militær og industriell infrastruktur dypt inne på russisk territorium.

Krigen i Ukraina

Russland invaderte Krim og deler av fylkene Luhansk og Donetsk i Øst-Ukraina i 2014. 24. februar 2022 gikk Russland til fullskala invasjon. Krigen medfører store militære tap og rammer sivile hardt.

articles.title: Politiet har skutt en mann i leilighet i Oslo
articles.content:
En mann er skutt av politiet i en leilighet etter en trusselsituasjon, og er kjørt til sykehus med uavklarte skader.

– Vi har også kontroll på en kvinne og en tredjemann som var i den aktuelle leiligheten, skriver operasjonsleder Rune Hekkelstrand i politiloggen.

– Verken disse to eller noen fra politiet er skadet. Det er mye politi i området og vil fortsatt være det utover formiddagen. Det er ikke fare for andre i området.

En mann er skutt av politiet etter at de rykket ut til melding om en trusselsituasjon på Lindeberg i Oslo.
